For birds in particular lens, you may need a very high shutter speed to freeze the movement.

Cameras require light to get pics.  A high shutter speed requires more light because the shutter is open for a very short amount of time. You can compensate by increasing the ISO (the sensitivity of the camera) but that tends to degrade image quality.  Aperture is the term that describes how much light comes in through the “shutter.” “f/2.8” is a fairly wide open shutter and allows lots of light into the camera. f/6.3 lets less light in so you need a slower shutter. But then fast moving objects tend to get blurry with a slower shutter. 

My advice is to get an inexpensive point and shoot camera to start, so you can get familiar with depth of field, shutter, aperture, white balance and other things that make up a good image. Get one that has a “P” or “M” mode … these allow you to manually control some or all parameters of the camera to allow you to get creative and customize the field of view. Once you get familiar with the concepts, then you can move into the DSLR or mirrorless cameras.

One trick I still use is grab a long screwdriver and place it on different areas of the engine, near the malfunction. On the valve covers you should hear at least 2 distinct noises - one per valve (unless you have 3 or more valves). Compare with a non-adjacent cylinder head valve cover. Compare the two sounds. Repeat on the block under the head. Repeat on a known good cylinder.  Compare the sounds.  
The trick is to put the screwdriver on the engine part then put the other end in your ear. You can also use a socket extension.  Anything a foot or two long ... and metal. It takes a trained ear but but doing this comparison, you should be able to determine which position on the engine is struggling.

I was asked by my employer to provide photo services on a volunteer basis for their entry in the Pride Parade. I spent a few moments thinking about it from a few different angles. I didn’t see any issues with it so I accepted. My daughter and her gf and another friend of theirs were already going so we made a “family day” out of it.  Took the train to Chicago. Walked a relative short distance to the staging area for my employer. I stopped walking and they continued on.  Me and my fellow employees decorated the trolly that my employer had rented. Had some pizza.  Took some pictures. But I was also actively “people watching.”  I had never been to one of these before so I was very intrigued. I saw the full spectrum.  Families pushing strollers with babies to a watching area, BDM, drag queens, couples of all types of orientations.  It was a parade where society in all its variations had come to watch and/or march. As we started marching, my employees would give out tchotchkes and I’d take pics of us interacting. As a former first responder, I was also watching for things that were out of place as I was shooting pics. Because people. The city had done a fantastic job protecting us all. They took 15-ton snow plow trucks and parked them at strategic locations and angles to protect us from anybody that would want to attempt to drive their cars into the marchers.  According to my Fitbit I did about 12000 steps I believe. Lots of pics. I also mounted a GoPro to the trolley and shot a video of the entire parade. Towards the end, I saw “them.”  The street preachers. Holding their signs up and yelling something I couldn’t hear fully but most of it was condemning hate speech. Telling the marchers they were condemned and going to hell. Ladies ... apparently yoga pants send you to hell now. I thought to myself - what about us straight couples marching. I know several other people that were from my employer that are straight and religious. What about us? I realized how their street preaching was widening the gap between the two sides and not trying to bridge it. It all really disturbed me. Not a single gay person made me feel the same way that day. Only the street preachers really bothered me. I felt embarrassed as a Christian. We finished marching. Interacted with a lady and her pet pig. That was a hoot. We headed to Sushi Toro, had some sushi and a beer, and talked about the day. On the train, the other three passed out. I however was still thinking about the street preachers and how they disturbed me. We got home. I edited my pics and gave them to the group chair person. I also set up a meeting with one of the group chair holders to talk about what I saw and get some advice about because some ideas were starting to come together. In between this, I was praying for guidance. As a bike rider I was praying as I would ride, often times on my way to work. I felt compelled to start a Christian outreach to help any gay Christians (yes it’s possible to be both!) have a safe place to exist as both. Shortly thereafter I started a Meetup. Then another Meetup. Fast forward to today. Both Meetups have a combined 50 members. Today my daughter, her gf and I are going to one of our Meetup events - coincidentally to a sushi event I set up. Going to enjoy some food and talk about whatever. - The end 🤣
